result.name: Graphline — native-ESM strangler for Apex 26 (zero build step)
result.thesis: The repo's founding bet ("the file you edit is the file the browser runs") is worth keeping; what must die is the hand-maintained substitute for a compiler. Native ES modules make the import graph the load-order authority (retiring tools/manifest.cjs FULL/HARD_EDGES/DEFERRED_EDGES), `tsc --checkJs --noEmit` makes module boundaries checker-enforced instead of conventional (retiring "every boundary is a discipline"), and a generated import map becomes the one place `?v=N` lives (retiring the sed-across-index.html bump). The key enabling fact: `defer` classic scripts and `type="module"` scripts execute in shared document order after parse, so each of the ~156 IIFEs converts one file per PR by swapping its own tag in place — converted modules `expose()` their global through a bridge shim so every unconverted IIFE, every `GLX.*`-patching spec, and `window.__apex` keep working at every intermediate commit. The G god-object is dissolved into typed domain state stores with the façade kept as a ratcheted compatibility shim; the renderer descriptor-copy becomes a real RendererPort with an explicit capability table. Because most historical damage came from parallel agents drifting out of sync, every retired prose/manifest invariant is replaced by either the module system itself or a generated-file-plus-guard pair — never by convention.
result.moduleSystem: Native ES modules, zero build. (1) SOURCE FORM: each IIFE becomes a module with named exports; `"use strict"` headers drop (implicit); one file = one module, same paths. Internal imports are RELATIVE (`import { TrackSpline } from "./spline.js"`), never bare — so the game boots even on browsers without import-map support. (2) VERSIONING: the existing inline `<script type="importmap">` (already there for vendor/three-0.184.0) grows a generated section mapping each module URL to its `?v=N` form ("./js/track/spline.js" → "./js/track/spline.js?v=43") — import maps remap URL-like specifiers, not just bare ones. `tools/gen-importmap.mjs` (checked-in output, like manifest today — a generator is not a build step) rewrites that block plus version.json; `.claude/skills/bump-cache` becomes "run the tool". Browsers without import maps degrade to un-busted module URLs, covered by sw.js build-named caches + the existing shell version guard (GitHub Pages max-age=600 bounds staleness at 10 min). (3) LOAD ORDER: during migration, tags stay per-file — classic tags get `defer`, converted tags become `type="module"` in place, document order preserved. End state: one `<script type="module" src="js/game.js?v=N">`; the graph is the order. Circuit order stops being tag order: `js/circuits/index.js` exports the curated 40-entry array (24 season rounds first — the stored `apex26.track` positional index contract moves into an explicit, tested array). DEFERRED backends become honest dynamic `import()` of `js/render/webgpu/wgx.js` / `three/tlx.js` module graphs — the DEFERRED map, DEFERRED_EDGES, and game.js's BACKEND_FILES table all die. (4) sw.js precache: derived from a generated, committed `precache.json` (tools/gen-precache.mjs walks the import graph from the entry), asserted against `git ls-files js/**` by a new guard. (5) TYPES: JSDoc typedefs + `jsconfig.json` + `tsc --checkJs --noEmit` in ci.yml over an allowlist that grows one file per conversion (never big-bang); espree is already a devDep for the import-hygiene lint. (6) BRIDGE: `js/bridge.js` exports `expose(name, api)` (sets `window[name]` — required, because module top-level bindings are invisible to classic scripts, unlike classic-script `const`s) and `legacy(name)` (typed getter over `window[name]` for reading a not-yet-converted global from a converted module; the import-hygiene guard forbids raw `window.X` reads outside bridge.js and ratchets `legacy()` call count to zero as migration completes). Node consumers (verify-track.cjs, foundation tests, carview) drop their VM script-loader for native `import()` in a child process per track (module-cache isolation), deleting manifest TRACK_VM/CARVIEW.
result.stateDesign: Dissolve G into ~8 typed domain stores under js/state/, each a module exporting one mutable plain object plus its effectful setters — no proxies, no event bus, no getter magic (determinism and grep-ability over cleverness): `race.js` (state/flow/session/paused/frozen/raceT/lapsTarget/seed — with `setFlow()` as the ONLY flow writer, keeping its Career notification), `tuning.js` (the game.js `let` tunables: PACE/DRIFT/FRONT_GRIP/ROAD_FOLLOW/STEER_*, with `setPace()` carrying the GameCams vmax re-inject side effect that today hides in G's setter), `camera.js` (camEye/camTgt/camFov/camMode/camCutT/dbgCam), `atmo.js` (raceTimeOfDay/raceWeather/weatherArc/_cloudBase/_lt*), `garage.js` (teamIdx/driverIdx/setupPreview*/livDraftOverride), `timing.js` (sector*, tt*), `net.js` (netPlay/netStart/netRoom/countT/lightsLit), `debug.js` (headlessMode/hideMeshes/_testInput/_studioRig). Cross-slice invariant writes stay named functions exported by the owning store. What does NOT move: `updateCar()`/`render()` locals and the ~40 interdependent tyre-model temporaries — physics-characterization.spec.js pins bit-stable laps and the review explicitly forbids carving those up; `cars[]`/`player`/`track` stay owned by game.js and are handed out by reference. PhysicsConsts stays a frozen data module. TRANSITION: `js/game/g-facade.js` exports `createG()` assembling today's exact G surface from the stores, so every `Module.create(G)` signature is untouched on day one; each js/game module then migrates to importing its store slices directly, and a new `tests/g-ratchet.test.mjs` counts façade members and only goes down — mechanizing the review's warning that G is "a migration device left in place as an architecture". JSDoc typedefs in js/state/types.js give tsc the shapes, so a module touching a slice it didn't import is a type error, not a convention violation. End state: G is gone; modules receive `{stores they need, helpers}` explicitly, and the "boundary crossings, not line count" extraction ranking becomes measurable as import edges.
result.rendererSeam: A real port interface replacing descriptor-copy. `js/render/port.js` defines `@typedef {Object} RendererPort` — the ~40-member contract transcribed from gfx.js's header, which is already the de-facto spec — plus a `caps` table: `{ textureArray, gpuTimer, msaa, pcss, volumetrics, hdr }`. Each backend module (`glx.js`, `webgpu/wgx.js`, `three/tlx.js`) carries `/** @implements {RendererPort} */`, so tsc fails on a missing member at check time — retiring the entire "GLX live function closing over a null gl" failure class that backend-surface-parity.test.mjs exists to catch, because installation stops copying members onto the GLX object entirely: `Gfx.create()` returns the selected port and game.js/Tracks.build pass that handle down (the M10 `opts.gfx` wiring already did the engine half). Feature checks change from `if (gfx.member)` — the trap that bit twice — to `if (gfx.caps.textureArray)`; a new caps-honesty spec asserts each declared cap by exercising it once per backend. Object-identity compatibility for the ~8 specs that monkey-patch `GLX.*` (webgl-probes, parts-mesh-cache, custom-team, lighting-ab, …): during migration, on backend selection game.js sets `window.GLX = port` (ALIAS, not member copy), preserving `gfx === GLX` on every path; those specs are then migrated one-by-one to a sanctioned `__apex.gfx()` handle, after which the alias remains only for GLX-default boots and is documented as one of exactly three deliberate globals (`__apex`, `GLX`, `Log`). TLX/WGX stay dynamic-import module graphs behind `Gfx.create()`'s never-throw null→GLX-fallback contract, unchanged. WGX stays frozen; its caps table finally states its non-parity (no volumetrics/PCSS/MSAA/gpuTimer/textureArray) as machine-readable truth instead of doc prose.

S1: add `defer` to every classic <script> tag in index.html (execution order and semantics preserved; this is what lets a module tag later slot into document order), bump via gen-importmap once it exists — for now the old ?v sed. Run test:tiny + smoke + pwa group (sw.js tag parser must still see the tags).

S2 (infrastructure, still zero behavior change): land js/bridge.js, js/render/port.js typedef, jsconfig.json + empty tsc allowlist + ci.yml job, tools/gen-importmap.mjs + tools/gen-precache.mjs writing committed outputs, and the three new guards (importmap.test.mjs, import-hygiene.test.mjs, circuit-order.test.mjs stub). Full suite: smoke, api, physics-characterization, track-foundation, pwa, net.

S12 (close-out): import-hygiene's legacy() ratchet driven to zero, expose() calls removed except __apex/GLX/Log/LightPresets, tsc allowlist == repo, docs pass (ARCHITECTURE.md, ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md §1, CLAUDE.md conventions, TESTING.md, bump-cache skill rewrite) gated by docs-integrity; migrate the 8 GLX-patching specs to __apex.gfx().
risks: Determinism drift: module evaluation reorders side effects (Log config, seed init, self-init modules) relative to today's tag order — mitigated by in-place tag swaps preserving document order and physics-characterization after every step, but a silent RNG-stream shift in S9/S10 is the single scariest failure; the existing gridUp()-sorts-with-simRnd() defect means characterization must pin quali/grid paths too, not just laps.

Support-floor raise: import maps need iOS 16.4+/Chrome 89+. Mitigated by relative-URL imports (the game runs without the map; the map only adds ?v busting) — but the degraded path leans on sw.js + the shell version guard for freshness, and non-SW first-visit users on stale Pages CDN get up to 10 min of mixed-version risk that the uniform-?v rule currently prevents. Must be tested deliberately (pwa group) before S11.

The defer/module document-order interleaving assumption is spec-correct but must be proven in the SwiftShader Playwright harness in S1 before anything depends on it; a harness quirk here invalidates the whole one-file-at-a-time strategy.

Parallel-agent races on shared generated files (importmap block, precache.json, tsc allowlist) recreate the historical unsynchronized-bulk-change failure mode — mitigation is hard rules: one conversion PR per file, generators are deterministic and re-runnable, guards fail loudly on divergence, and worktree discipline per docs/PARALLEL-WORK.md; mid-test-run version bumps stay forbidden.

The ~8 GLX-monkey-patching specs during S7: alias-not-copy preserves object identity only if sequenced exactly with gfx.js conversion; getting it wrong turns lighting-ab/parts-mesh-cache red in confusing ways.

Node module cache vs per-circuit isolation: S3's child-process-per-track import() is slower than today's VM reuse; verify-track's 2 s promise may degrade and must be re-measured before agents rely on it in edit loops.

tsc --checkJs over IIFE-era code will surface hundreds of latent nits (implicit any, window expandos, the catalogued dead exports); the per-file allowlist prevents a big-bang but sustained discipline is needed to keep it growing rather than stalling.

sw.js precache derivation change (tag parsing → precache.json) risks bricking installed PWAs on the transition build if the version guard misfires — needs a dedicated upgrade test crossing the boundary build.

Scope seams: converted modules no longer share the classic global lexical environment, so any IIFE secretly reading another file's top-level const via bare identifier (not via a documented global) breaks at that file's conversion — S0's import-graph truth check exists precisely to find these before they bite.
result.costEstimate: ~155 conversion PRs plus ~15 infrastructure/guard PRs. Leaf and data files (shaders, tables, circuits, net, data tabs — roughly 100 files) are mechanical: 30–60 min each including the pick-tests groups; engine/renderer/game files (~30) are 2–6 h each; S6 (circuits), S7 (renderer alias flip), S9 (state stores), and S11 (the entry flip) are the four heavy steps at 1–2 focused days each. Wall-clock is dominated by SwiftShader browser-group runtime, not editing — with 2–3 parallel agent worktrees respecting the 4-core box, the whole strangler lands in roughly 10–14 weeks of steady background work, and every step is independently shippable, so it can pause indefinitely at any green point with the bridge shim carrying the mixed world. Payoff begins early: HARD_EDGES rows start dying in week 1, and tsc coverage compounds per file rather than arriving at the end.

result.name: Typed Apex — esbuild + TypeScript, contracts as types
result.thesis: The no-build bet stops paying the moment the maintainer is a population of parallel AI agents instead of one human with muscle memory. The bet bought "the file you edit is the file the browser runs"; the price is that every consistency property a compiler gives for free is re-implemented as a hand-built guard: tools/manifest.cjs + HARD_EDGES + tests/load-order.test.mjs are a hand-rolled import graph; 164 hand-bumped ?v=N URLs + version.json (and the bump-cache skill, and the "never bump mid-run" hazard) are hand-rolled content hashing; the 200+-entry G façade with its documented drift bugs (the dead countT accessor, the dead duplicate setLightTune key) is a hand-rolled typed interface; backend-surface-parity.test.mjs's "explicit undefined" rule is a hand-rolled mapped type; the 107-member scenery contract test is a hand-rolled interface freeze. ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md's own governing law — "what a test asserts stays true; what only prose says drifts" — is an argument FOR a compiler: a type is an assertion checked on every keystroke of every parallel session, which is exactly the synchronization mechanism agents drifting apart need. The fix is deliberately minimal: esbuild (invoked from tools/build.mjs, fitting the repo's tools/ culture) + tsc --noEmit as a guard, no framework, no Vite dev-server dual-semantics, ES2022 target, no minification until physics-characterization proves it safe. What breaks is named and compensated: the edit-is-run property is replaced by <100 ms watch rebuilds plus per-file sourcemaps shipped to Pages; the ?v=N scheme is replaced by build-written content hashes feeding the same shell version guard; window globals and window.__apex are kept alive by an explicit compatibility module so all 111 Playwright specs (including the 8 that monkey-patch GLX.*) stay green untouched. The migration is leaf-first and per-domain, with exactly one mechanical, script-verified cutover (IIFE→ESM codemod emitting byte-diffable per-file IIFE output) gated by the full suite and the bit-stable physics characterization.
result.moduleSystem: ES modules in src/ (mirroring the current js/ domain layout), compiled by esbuild driven from tools/build.mjs; typescript's tsc runs --noEmit as the type guard (esbuild strips, tsc checks — builds stay ~200 ms for 156 files). Each current IIFE becomes a module whose single global becomes its named export (src/track/spline.ts exports TrackSpline). One generated compatibility module, src/globals.ts, imports every module and assigns window.Log, window.GLX, window.Tracks, window.TrackDefs, … — this is a PUBLISHED, test-asserted surface, not a shim to delete: the Playwright specs, the __apex console workflow, and tools/agent.mjs all reach page globals, and keeping them is nearly free. Load order: eval-time HARD_EDGES become literal import statements (the codemod seeds them from manifest.cjs and fails loudly on cycles); the curated circuit order — which is product data (Tracks.LIST == picker/season order), not a load-order artifact — survives as src/circuits/index.ts, an explicit ordered import list that registers each circuit, keeping "a stored apex26.track is a positional index" true. DEFERRED backends become real dynamic import() chunks via esbuild code-splitting, deleting the hand-rolled injector and the three-way DEFERRED/BACKEND_FILES/sw.js agreement: sw.js's optional precache and version.json are generated from esbuild's metafile by tools/build.mjs. Vendored three r184 stays vendored (supply-chain stability) behind an esbuild alias replacing the importmap. index.html stays hand-authored static DOM except a marked script block tools/build.mjs rewrites (the same shape as today's bump-cache sed, but automatic and hash-based). Node-VM consumers (verify-track.cjs, TRACK_VM tests, tools/carview.html) switch from VM-eval of manifest subsets to direct ESM imports / their own tiny esbuild entries — faster and simpler than today. Migration-interim mode: the build can emit per-file IIFE dist/js/*.js with today's filenames and global names (esbuild --format=iife --global-name per file), so the ESM cutover commit changes zero bytes of index.html and keeps load-order.test.mjs passing until the bundle flip retires it.
result.stateDesign: Three moves, none touching render()/updateCar() internals (the determinism spec forbids carving them up, and ARCHITECTURE.md is right that the tyre model's ~40 interdependent locals must stay one integration). (1) Type the façade first: src/game/ctx.d.ts declares interface GameCtx — every one of the ~200 G members with real types and readonly where the code means read-only (G.ranked, G.cars, the setupPreview* getters). Every js/game/* module's create(G: GameCtx) is checked immediately under checkJs via JSDoc, before any renaming to .ts. This single interface retires the façade-drift defect class the review documents (dead expandos like the old countT, dead duplicate keys, modules reading members G never carried): an agent adding a G member must edit the interface, and an agent reading a nonexistent one gets a compile error in its own session instead of a runtime undefined in someone else's. (2) Then execute the already-planned "pass 2" under type cover: promote game.js closure lets, domain by domain (sky state, sector timing, camera state, tt state — the accessor clusters visible at lines 2540-2772), into a typed GameState object that G's getters become plain references to; tunables stay mutable per the PhysicsConsts split; the module-size ratchet keeps being lowered on each extraction. (3) Extraction candidates keep being ranked by boundary crossings exactly as the review prescribes — but now a crossing is a typed interface member, so the garage-live-preview extraction (blocked today on 15 undeclared crossings) becomes tractable: define the car-drawing seam as an interface, and tsc enforces that render() and the garage consume the same one. PACE discipline: vstd-lint stays (it is semantic, not structural); a future branded type (type ScaledSpeed = number & {__scaled}) is the eventual typed replacement but is explicitly NOT in this plan's critical path.
result.rendererSeam: src/render/backend.d.ts declares interface RendererBackend — the ~40-member contract currently prose in gfx.js's header (init/resize/createMesh/createChunkedMesh/begin/draw/drawSky/drawShadow/drawParticles/mobileTier/createTextureArray/gpuTimer/…). GLX implements it fully as the reference. WGX and TLX are typed as type BackendSurface = { [K in keyof RendererBackend]: RendererBackend[K] | undefined } — the mapped type IS backend-surface-parity.test.mjs's "absent members declared as explicit undefined" rule, enforced at compile time: a backend cannot silently omit a member and inherit GLX's live function closing over a null gl (the exact bug that bit twice). The parity test is retired only after all three backends are TS-checked; until then both run. Deferred loading becomes esbuild dynamic-import chunks selected by the same apex26.gfxBackend key inside Gfx.create() — a failed chunk fetch resolves to null → GLX fallback, preserving today's honest degradation. The descriptor-copy install onto the GLX object is RETAINED deliberately as the object-identity compatibility contract for the ~8 specs that monkey-patch GLX.* (webgl-probes, parts-mesh-cache, custom-team, lighting-ab, …): GLX stays a mutable object export aliased onto window, gfx === GLX on every path, exactly as the TLX M10 wiring documents. Tracks.build keeps taking opts.gfx (typed RendererBackend). The known cross-backend shading divergences (TLX wet-surface model, the GLSL-only MIRROR id 27) are renderer-parity work the type system cannot see — flagged as out of scope so nobody mistakes "typed" for "at parity". WGX stays frozen and typed Partial-explicit.

risks: The Phase 2 codemod is the largest single change in the repo's history — the exact shape (unsynchronized bulk change) that caused its historical damage. Mitigation: it is scripted and re-runnable, verified by AST-equivalence diff of the per-file IIFE output, gated by the full suite + bit-stable physics, and executed in a drained window with every parallel session stopped; if the gate fails, the commit is dropped, not patched forward.

Determinism drift from esbuild transforms or a future minifier reordering float expressions — physics-characterization.spec.js is the tripwire at every phase; minification stays off until it proves safe, and stays off forever if it does not.

Boot-timing semantics change: classic scripts execute during parse, the module graph executes deferred — anything implicitly relying on script-tag timing (self-init modules like sheetshape/topmodal/menunav observing DOM, the Log-loads-first guarantee, sw registration order) can shift. The Log guarantee is restructured as 'every module imports log', which is stronger; smoke/menu/ui groups catch the rest, but this is the likeliest source of one-off flakes at Phase 3.

The window-globals compatibility surface could rot into 'two ways to reach everything' and tempt agents to keep writing global reads in src/. Compensation: an eslint rule (no-restricted-globals against the registry) makes src/ import-only; window.* is written exactly once in src/globals.ts and consumed only by tests/devtools.

Sourcemapped debugging on SwiftShader/Playwright and on phones is worse than editing the served file directly — honest loss. Compensated by <100 ms watch rebuilds, shipped .map files on Pages, and the fact that the primary debugging surface here is __apex/Log, which is unaffected — but an agent mid-incident will feel the extra indirection.

Agent-instruction lag: dozens of skills and docs (bump-cache, check-changes, playwright-probe, PARALLEL-WORK) encode the no-build workflow; any session running on stale instructions after Phase 2/3 will hand-bump hashes or edit dist/. Every phase commit must update CLAUDE.md and the affected skills atomically, and dist/ must be gitignored so an edit there is loudly wrong.

tsc over a half-JS half-TS 156-file graph can produce noisy any-poisoning that agents 'fix' with as-casts, laundering the very drift the migration exists to catch. Mitigation: checkJs rolls out per-file, a no-explicit-any lint ratchet (same pattern as silent-catch), and GameCtx/RendererBackend/SceneryApi authored as precise interfaces before any consumer converts.

Import cycles that today's global-plus-call-time indirection tolerates (game ↔ modules via G, tracks.js's GLX fallback) could force awkward refactors at codemod time; the G runtime injection actually removes most, but any survivor must be broken by type-only imports or a deliberate late-binding seam, never by weakening the graph back to window reads.

GitHub Pages/PWA cutover: the first hashed-URL deploy must interact correctly with the old sw.js installed on players' phones (old precache paths vanish). The shell version guard handles the force-refresh, but the Phase 3 deploy needs a staged rollout check on a real installed PWA before the branch push.
result.costEstimate: Roughly 25-35 agent-days spread over 4-6 weeks of sessions, front-loaded on safety tooling rather than conversion: Phase 0 ~2 days (globals.d.ts + GameCtx transcription is the big authoring task), Phase 1 ~1 day, Phase 2 ~4-6 days (codemod ~2, verification tooling ~2, the gated cutover window ~1), Phase 3 ~2-3 days including real-device PWA validation, Phase 4 ~12-18 days (156 files, mostly mechanical at 5-10 files/day, parallelizable by domain once tsc arbitrates cross-session consistency — the first time parallel agent work here has a synchronizer stronger than the test suite), Phase 5 ongoing at the existing extraction cadence. CI cost: +5-10 s per run (tsc --noEmit + esbuild), negligible against the SwiftShader browser groups. Payback: retires the manifest/tag/HARD_EDGES bookkeeping, the entire cache-bump ritual, and the façade-drift, backend-parity, and circuit-field-typo defect classes — several of which appear in ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md §7 today — while converting the two-place-consistency problem (the root cause of most historical agent damage) from hand-maintained guards into compiler errors delivered inside the session that creates them.

result.name: Bedrock: the Hardened IIFE Plan (guards become the compiler)
result.thesis: The IIFE+globals architecture is not the problem — unsynchronized bulk change by parallel agents is, and every catalogued defect class (hand-maintained load order, G-façade expandos like the netStartArm countT bug, descriptor-copy zombie members, mirror-comment drift, the unguarded arc invariant) is a missing observation, not a missing module system. So keep the founding bet — the file you edit is the file the browser runs, which is uniquely valuable when the maintainers are agents debugging live pages — and finish the repo's own governing law ("what a test asserts stays true; what only prose says drifts") by converting every remaining prose invariant into a generator or a guard. Three mechanisms do the compiler's job without a compiler: (1) tsc --checkJs in script mode, which natively type-checks cross-file global references across no-module files — the IIFE architecture is accidentally the ONE architecture TypeScript can check with zero migration; (2) a generated manifest whose HARD_EDGES are derived by espree/eslint-scope (already devDeps) from actual eval-time destructures, so load order stops being hand-remembered; (3) G dissolved into six sealed, owned state objects with a frozen surface snapshot, so the façade stops being "game.js's closure with extra steps". This beats ESM on payoff-per-risk because ESM is a big-bang class change that invalidates the safety net's own foundations (the 8 GLX-monkey-patching specs, the descriptor-copy identity contract, sw.js's tag-parsing precache, verify-track's VM loader, the carview subset) while buying only an import graph we can generate and assert more cheaply; and it beats full TS because checkJs delivers ~80% of the defect-catching (the two-place-consistency hole) at zero runtime diff, per-file incrementality, and full reversibility, versus renaming 156 files, adding a build step that breaks GitHub Pages purity, and rewriting every path-reading tool. For a fan game maintained by parallel agents, migrations are the risk surface; guards are the payoff surface. This plan is all guard, no migration.
result.moduleSystem: UNCHANGED at runtime: every file stays a "use strict" IIFE assigning exactly one global, loaded by script tags, zero runtime deps, GitHub Pages static. What changes is that the module system's invariants become machine-derived. (a) GENERATED MANIFEST: tools/gen-manifest.mjs becomes the writer; tools/manifest.cjs, the index.html script-tag block, and sw.js's DEFERRED precache seed become its three outputs. Inputs: a per-file header declaration (`/* @global GameHud @after GameTables(eval) */`) plus an espree/eslint-scope scan (tools/scan-globals.mjs) that detects eval-time global destructures (`const {x} = SomeGlobal` at IIFE top level) and derives HARD_EDGES automatically — the hand list is retired after a transition assertion proves derived ⊇ hand-written. Call-time-but-pinned edges (the js/net/ family, career→quali) stay in a small hand-curated CALL_EDGES list since they are not statically visible; the curated CIRCUITS calendar array stays hand-owned data (it IS Tracks.LIST order, a product decision). A drift test in test:tooling-fast asserts regeneration is a byte-identical no-op, so tests/load-order.test.mjs's job shrinks from "did a human keep three copies in sync" to "did you run the generator". gen-manifest never touches ?v=N — bump-cache stays the sole version writer. (b) GLOBAL REGISTRY GUARD: tests/global-registry.test.mjs asserts, from the same scan, that every js/ file assigns exactly its one declared global and reads only globals some file declares — a linker for the globals architecture. It replaces the "grep the removed symbol names after every extraction" habit that has caught leftovers three-for-three by hand. (c) TYPED JSDOC IN CI: jsconfig.json scoped to js/** (vendor/ excluded), `tsc --noEmit --checkJs` as npm run typecheck in ci.yml. Because these files are scripts (no import/export), tsc puts their top-level globals in one shared global scope — cross-file surface checking works natively. types/globals.d.ts declares surfaces for un-annotated globals; files opt in with // @ts-check; tests/ts-check-ratchet.test.mjs ratchets the opted-in count up and the tsc error baseline down, same idiom as module-size.test.mjs. TypeScript is a devDependency only, like Playwright — the runtime stays dependency-free.
result.stateDesign: Dissolve G's ~140 flat members into six sealed, singly-owned state objects created in game.js's closure, with G retained as a thin delegating façade during migration so no consumer or spec breaks mid-flight. The domains, drawn from the actual G region (js/game.js ~2540-2772): S.cam (camEye/camTgt/camFov/camMode/camRoll/camCutT/dbgCam, photoMode/photoAlt/photoVertT — writers: cameras.js, cam-modes.js, cam-tune.js, photomode.js); S.tuning (the mutable physics lets: DRIFT, FRONT_GRIP, PACE, PLAYER_GRIP, ROAD_FOLLOW, STEER_*, WHEELBASE, YAW_* — writers: steer-tuning.js, apex.js; immutables stay in PhysicsConsts); S.race (state, flow/session, raceT, raceLaps, lapsTarget, ranked, sector*, countT, lightsLit, raceQuali, raceReliability, ttRecord family — writers: game.js, netplay-via-game seams); S.world (track, trackIdx, builtTrackNight, raceTimeOfDay, raceWeather, weatherArc, skyT, _cloudBase, _lt* — writers: atmosphere.js, light-store.js, game.js); S.garage (teamIdx, driverIdx, setupPreview*, livDraftOverride, _spMeshKey — writers: setup-ui.js, menus.js); S.debug (headlessMode, hideMeshes, frozen, _testInput, _studioRig, skyViewOverride — writer: apex.js). Rules made mechanical, not aspirational: (1) every S object is Object.seal()ed at construction, which kills the silent-expando class outright — the netStartArm G.countT expando documented in game.js would have been a TypeError in strict mode on day one; (2) state objects are dumb data — any write with a side effect (G's PACE setter re-initing GameCams, raceAeroMode repainting the button) becomes a named verb (setPace(), setAeroMode()) on G, never a property setter, so reading code can never trigger hidden work; (3) ownership is a checked table, not prose: docs/STATE-OWNERSHIP.md lists writer-modules per domain and tests/state-ownership.test.mjs asserts it from the eslint-scope scan (a non-owner writing S.cam.* fails CI); (4) the whole G+S surface is a frozen contract — tests/g-contract.test.mjs snapshots member names and kinds (get/set/fn) exactly like scenery-api-contract.test.mjs freezes its 107 names, so widening the façade is a deliberate, reviewable snapshot edit (the exact discipline the garage-preview extraction analysis in ARCHITECTURE.md called for); (5) a flat-member-count ratchet on G shrinks it as consumers migrate from G.camEye to S.cam.eye. Determinism constraint honored: render()/updateCar() bodies and their ~40 interdependent locals are untouched — only lets already published through G move, and physics-characterization.spec.js gates every carve.
result.rendererSeam: Formalize the port as data while keeping descriptor-copy as the compatibility contract. (1) New js/render/port.js (global GfxPort, loads before glx.js): `{ VERSION, MEMBERS: [~40 names], OPTIONAL: ["gpuTimer","createTextureArray","volumetrics-caps",…] }` — the contract that today lives half in gfx.js's header comment and half in tests/backend-surface-parity.test.mjs moves into one runtime-readable object. (2) Gfx.install(backend) absorbs the descriptor-copy from game.js: it copies the backend's descriptors onto the GLX object (preserving the object-identity contract the ~8 GLX.*-patching specs and monkey-patch sites rely on — webgl-probes, parts-mesh-cache, custom-team, lighting-ab keep working unmodified), and MECHANIZES the zombie-member fix: any GfxPort.MEMBERS name the backend does not define is written as explicit `undefined` by the installer itself, instead of each backend author remembering the idiom that bit twice before backend-surface-parity pinned it. The parity test is rebased to derive its member list from GfxPort.MEMBERS (bidirectional: GLX must define every member, GfxPort must name every GLX public member), so the port cannot drift from its own contract. (3) types/gfx.d.ts declares the port interface once; GLX, TLX, WGX carry @implements, and tsc flags a signature divergence — the check backend-surface-parity structurally cannot do (it sees names, not shapes). (4) Honest capability flags replace silence: backends declare `caps: {msaa, pcss, volumetrics, matTex, gpuTimer}` in GfxPort terms, and __apex.info() reports them, so WGX's frozen non-parity is queryable rather than folklore. (5) The known cross-backend shading divergences (TLX's pre-fix wet model, the GLSL-only MIRROR id 27) get a tracking table in docs keyed to GfxPort.VERSION — parity work, explicitly out of this plan's scope, but now enumerated where docs-integrity can see it. Object.seal(G) breaking an unaudited expando writer: the netStartArm case proves expandos exist and are invisible until sealed; step 6's audit must grep-and-scan before sealing, and the seal must land alone (instantly bisectable) rather than inside a carve PR.

Determinism regression from S carves: moving a let behind a sealed-object property is behaviorally identical but touches game.js's hot closure; physics-characterization.spec.js gates every carve, and the plan deliberately never touches render()/updateCar() bodies — but a timeout-on-a-busy-box false negative could mask a real diff, so carve gates re-run solo per the TESTING.md rule before believing any red OR green.

# Final Recommendation: Harden the IIFE Architecture (Bedrock), with Typed Apex's interfaces and Graphline's dependency-truth scanner grafted in

## 1. The winning direction and why

**Bedrock wins, and it is not close: 43 + 44 = 87 combined, vs Graphline 64 (30+34) and Typed Apex 54 (27+27).** Both judges converged independently on the same reasoning, which is the strongest signal in the exercise:

- **Migration risk is the dominant axis for this repo, and Bedrock is the only plan that scores 9/9 on it from both judges.** The constraint list says the historical damage came from unsynchronized bulk change by parallel agents. Typed Apex's Phase 2 is — by its own admission — "the largest single change in the repo's history" requiring a drained-sessions freeze window, a coordination primitive a population of parallel agents demonstrably cannot execute. Graphline avoids the big bang but replaces it with a 10–14 week mixed IIFE/ESM world where ~170 PRs contend over shared generated files (importmap block, tsc allowlist) — a *new* cross-session contention surface. Bedrock's worst-case rollback at every single step is `git revert` of one PR with the 111-spec suite green on both sides.
- **Determinism: 9/9 for Bedrock vs 6/6 and 6/5.** Bedrock never routes physics bytes through a transpiler and never reorders eval relative to today's tag order; only `let`s already published through G move, gated by `tests/physics-characterization.spec.js` per carve.
- **The score gap where Bedrock loses — agentSafety (7 vs Typed Apex's 9) — is the one it can close by grafting.** Typed Apex's core insight is correct: the guards ARE a hand-rolled compiler, and a type error delivered inside the session that creates the drift is the synchronizer agents lack. Bedrock's own step 4 already gestures at this; the synthesis below adopts Typed Apex's interface-authoring verbatim, because **script-mode `tsc --checkJs` natively type-checks cross-file globals across no-module files** — the IIFE architecture is accidentally the one architecture TypeScript can check with zero migration. That captures ~80% of the compiler payoff at ~20% of the risk.
- **Bedrock is a no-regrets prefix of Graphline.** Its scanner is Graphline's S0; its typecheck is Graphline's tsc bootstrap. Nothing done here is thrown away if the repo later wants native ESM.

## 2. The synthesized architecture

**Base: Bedrock — the IIFE+globals runtime is unchanged; every remaining prose invariant becomes a generator or a guard.** Three grafts from the runners-up, all named "best idea" by at least one judge:

1. **From Typed Apex (graft into Phase 1, done first and most precisely): authored `.d.ts` contracts.** `types/globals.d.ts` (~30 core globals), `interface GameCtx` transcribed from the G region at `js/game.js:2540–2772`, `interface RendererBackend` (~40 members from gfx.js's header), `interface SceneryApi` (the 107 members `tests/scenery-api-contract.test.mjs` freezes). `tsc --noEmit --checkJs` in ci.yml; files opt in per-file with `// @ts-check`; an adoption ratchet test (same idiom as `tests/module-size.test.mjs`) keeps coverage monotonic. This retires the façade-drift defect class (the dead `countT` accessor, dead duplicate `setLightTune` key) in the session that creates it.
2. **From Graphline (graft into Phase 0): the dependency-truth check.** `tools/scan-globals.mjs` (espree/eslint-scope — both already devDeps at package.json:60–61) derives the real eval-time global graph and **asserts `tools/manifest.cjs` order is a valid topological sort and derived edges ⊇ the 5 hand-recorded HARD_EDGES entries** before anything moves. Zero product edits; surfaces every undeclared edge; keeps the door open for Graphline's proven in-place `defer`/`type=module` tag-swap strangler later.
3. **Bedrock's own sharpest mechanisms, kept exactly as designed:** generated manifest with byte-identical-first-run bootstrap (three outputs: manifest.cjs, index.html tag block, sw.js precache seed); `Object.seal()`ed single-owner state objects (S.cam/S.tuning/S.race/S.world/S.garage/S.debug) with side effects as named verbs, never property setters; the `g-contract` snapshot making façade widening a loud merge conflict between parallel sessions; and mechanized explicit-`undefined` backfill inside a centralized `Gfx.install()`, preserving `gfx === GLX` identity for the ~8 monkey-patching specs.

Explicitly out of scope, eyes open: `render()`/`updateCar()` internals (determinism spec forbids it), the ?v=N bump ritual, and the no-edits-mid-test-run hazard. The last two are the acknowledged Graphline-only wins; see §4.

## 3. Phased migration plan (every phase ends green; guard changes listed per phase)

All new guards must fit the ~15 s `test:tooling-fast` budget (all are static scans) and carry the vstd-lint-style in-place escape hatch — a guard agents `--force` around is worse than no guard.

**Phase 0 — Observe (no runtime bytes change, no cache bump).**
Land `tools/scan-globals.mjs` emitting `artifacts/dep-graph.json`; Graphline's toposort assertion against manifest order; `tests/global-registry.test.mjs` in baseline-ratchet mode (one declared global per file, no undeclared reads — replaces the "grep removed symbols" post-extraction ritual). Split manifest edges into derived EVAL_EDGES + hand-curated CALL_EDGES (net family, career→quali, with rationale comments).
*Guards added:* global-registry, toposort assertion. *Retired:* nothing. *Gate:* test:tooling-fast.

**Phase 1 — Types (Typed Apex graft; still zero runtime change).**
`jsconfig.json` (js/** only, vendor/ excluded), `types/globals.d.ts`, `GameCtx`, `RendererBackend`, `SceneryApi` authored as precise interfaces *before* any consumer opts in. First `// @ts-check` tranche: physics-consts, tables, light-store, racecontrol, aerozones, skidmarks. `npm run typecheck` in ci.yml + `tests/ts-check-ratchet.test.mjs`.
*Guards added:* typecheck job, ts-check ratchet. *Retired:* nothing yet — but façade-drift and "read a G member that doesn't exist" become compile errors for opted-in files. *Gate:* test:tooling-fast.

**Phase 2 — Generate the manifest.**
`tools/gen-manifest.mjs` consumes CIRCUITS (still hand-curated calendar data — it IS `Tracks.LIST`/picker order), per-file `@global` headers, and the scan; emits manifest.cjs FULL/DEFERRED, rewrites the marked index.html tag block, writes sw.js's optional precache seed. **First run must be byte-identical to committed files** (topo-sort seeded with current order). Regeneration-no-op drift test added. gen-manifest never touches ?v=N — bump-cache stays the sole version writer.
*Guards added:* regeneration drift test. *Retired:* **HARD_EDGES as a hand-maintained artifact; the three-way DEFERRED/BACKEND_FILES/sw.js hand agreement collapses to one drift check.** `tests/load-order.test.mjs` survives, now asserting "did you run the generator." *Gate:* test:tooling-fast + pwa group (background, per test-bg discipline).

**Phase 3 — Renderer port.**
`js/render/port.js` (GfxPort: VERSION/MEMBERS/OPTIONAL/caps) + `Gfx.install()` absorbing descriptor-copy from game.js with mechanized explicit-undefined backfill; `@implements` on GLX/TLX/WGX against `RendererBackend`; `__apex.info()` reports caps, making WGX's frozen non-parity machine-readable.
*Guards changed:* `tests/backend-surface-parity.test.mjs` rebased onto GfxPort.MEMBERS (its hardcoded roster retires; the file survives); the "explicit undefined" author discipline retires into installer code. *Gate:* pick-tests groups **plus all 8 GLX-patching specs** (webgl-probes, parts-mesh-cache, custom-team, lighting-ab, …) to prove the identity contract held. Bump ?v=N last.

**Phase 4 — Seal and carve state.**
Expando audit, then `Object.seal(G)` **landed alone** (instantly bisectable) + `tests/g-contract.test.mjs` snapshot. Then six single-domain PRs: S.cam first (lowest coupling), then S.tuning (side-effectful setters → named verbs `setPace()`/`setAeroMode()`; **full physics-characterization gate**), then S.garage, S.race, S.world, S.debug — characterization re-runs for S.race/S.world. `docs/STATE-OWNERSHIP.md` + `tests/state-ownership.test.mjs` (non-owner write fails CI). Consumers migrate G.camEye → S.cam.eye module-by-module; G's flat-member ratchet and the module-size ceiling go down together. A busy-box timeout is a measurement of the machine — re-run any red or green solo before believing it.
*Guards added:* g-contract, state-ownership, G flat-member ratchet. *Retired (gradually):* delegating G accessors; the silent-expando class dies at seal time. *Gate:* physics-characterization + pick-tests groups per carve; each carve branch lives under a week.

**Phase 5 — Close the review's named guard gaps.**
`tools/arc-lint.mjs` + `tests/arc-invariant.test.mjs` (allowlisted `Tracks.curvature()` sites tagged AI-only|assist-gated|broadcast-only|surface — promoting the PHYSICS.md table from prose to assertion); vertex-budget gate in verify-track (Vegas grandfathered, ratchet-down); the net-authority fix landed **with** its pinning spec in one PR; `test:agent` on a scheduled CI job.
*Guards added:* arc-invariant, vertex baseline, net-authority spec. *Retired:* the last "exactly the shape of thing that stops holding" prose invariants.

**Phase 6 — Continuous.** Expand `// @ts-check` in tranches (ratchet-enforced); type the S objects and GfxPort; rewrite ARCHITECTURE.md's reorg section (G = thin verb façade over six owned domains) under docs-integrity; TUNE_DEFS mirror-comments replaced by a checked mapping.

**Never retired, at any phase:** physics-characterization (the master gate), scenery-api-contract (until/unless SceneryApi typing of all 40 circuits fully subsumes it — keep both regardless, it's cheap), module-size, vstd-lint/invariant, graph-parity, docs-integrity, test-groups, deploy-staging, silent-catch, comment-citations, verify-track, and the pick-tests/test-bg operational discipline.

## 4. When NOT to do this

Do not run this plan if the repo's observed pain shifts to the two frictions Bedrock deliberately leaves standing: if post-mortems start showing that most agent damage comes from **the ?v=N bump ritual** (missed bumps, mid-run bumps force-reloading test pages) or **the js/-edit-during-a-browser-run mixed-build hazard**, then the correct move is Graphline's S0–S2 (defer tags + generated import map + bridge) — for which Phases 0–1 here are a direct prefix — not more guards; a guard cannot delete a workflow hazard, only police it. Likewise, if the parallel-agent population grows to the point where test-time checking is chronically too late (drift merged before any suite runs) and the owner can genuinely tolerate a toolchain on the deploy path, Typed Apex's compile-on-keystroke regime becomes worth its freeze-window risk — but only executed via Graphline's incremental strangler, never via the Phase-2 codemod. And if the honest trajectory is maintenance-mode (a finished fan game with occasional track edits), stop after Phase 2: the scanner, the typed interfaces, and the generated manifest are the 80% payoff; sealing and carving G is only worth it while active extraction work continues. Finally, if any new guard cannot stay inside the ~15 s tooling-fast budget or starts getting `--force`'d, delete it — guard fatigue converts this plan's payoff surface into its failure mode.
